analyst_view.overall: Early view: Milan play this four days after a Europa League trip to Olympiacos, and they had a long injury list before the break (Pavlovic, Tomori, Gabbia, Chukwueze, Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers). Amorim's side take few shots but score from them. Cagliari ended a four-game losing run by beating Frosinone with a compact, counter-attacking display, and their home games have been very low-scoring.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Cagliari's home games have averaged only 1.4 goals, among the lowest home figures in the league, and Caprile is in form. Milan may rotate after Olympiacos, and they keep the ball rather than chase goals.

corners.text: The site expects 9.0 corners. Cagliari's home games have averaged almost 12 corners, nearly eight of them conceded, but Milan's games are the lowest-corner games in the league. Those cancel out, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards. I lean higher: Milan have been booked about 2.8 times a game away, and collected four bookings at Genoa. Cagliari's home games have averaged about 3.5 cards.

shots.text: The site expects 24.8 shots. Cagliari's home games have averaged about 31, but almost all of those are opponents' shots, and Milan's away games average about 24. I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target, close to both Cagliari's home average and Milan's away average. Nothing points either way.
